style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A psalm of the separated man. David asks to be judged -- not spared but tried: examine me, test me, refine my heart and my kidneys -- and then lays out the evidence. Covenant love before his eyes, a walk in God's truth; no seat with worthless men, no entry among the concealed, hatred for the assembly of evildoers; hands washed in innocence and a circuit around the altar, loud with thanksgiving. The center is a love song to a building: O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory has its tent. Then the fear behind it all -- do not sweep my soul away with sinners and men of blood, whose right hands are stuffed with bribes -- and the resolve: as for me, I will walk in my integrity. But the integrity psalm still ends by asking to be ransomed and shown grace, and its last line is not a courtroom but a congregation: my foot stands on level ground, and in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.

1.text: Of David. Judge me and clear me, O LORD, for I have walked in my integrity; I have trusted in the LORD, and I shall not waver.
1.amp: A Psalm of David. Judge [shaphat -- vindicate] me, O LORD [YHWH]; for I have walked [halak] in mine integrity [tom -- wholeness]: I have trusted [batach] also in the LORD [YHWH]; therefore I shall not slide [maad -- waver].
1.notes: shophteni YHWH (H8199, H3068): JUDGE me -- not a plea for leniency but for a verdict; David wants the case heard. ki-ani be-tummi halakhti (H8537, H1980): because I have walked in my tom, my integrity, the wholeness of Job 1:1; u-ba-YHWH batachti lo emad (H982, H4571): and in the LORD I have trusted, I will not waver. Integrity and trust in one breath: the psalm's innocence is not self-made.

2.text: Examine me, O LORD, and put me to the proof; refine my inmost self and my heart.
2.amp: Examine [bachan -- assay] me, O LORD [YHWH], and prove [nasah -- test] me; try [tsaraph -- refine] my reins [kilyah -- kidneys, inmost self] and my heart [leb].
2.notes: bechaneni YHWH ve-nasseni (H974, H3068, H5254): assay me and test me -- tsarphah khilyotai ve-libbi (H6884, H3629, H3820): REFINE my kidneys and my heart, the seat of feeling and the seat of will, the two organs the Hebrew uses for the whole inner man. He invites the assay of Psalm 11:4-5 -- the same bachan, the LORD's eyelids testing the righteous: a man who asks to be smelted is not hiding slag.

3.text: For Your covenant love is right before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth.
3.amp: For Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] is before mine eyes [ayin]: and I have walked [halak] in Your truth [emeth -- faithfulness].
3.notes: ki-chasdekha le-neged enai (H2617, H5869): Your chesed, Your covenant love, kept in front of my eyes -- the ground of the integrity, stated before the integrity is described -- ve-hithallakhti ba-amittekha (H1980, H571): and I have walked about in Your emeth, Your truth. The two words of Exodus 34:6 as the two rails of a life.

4.text: I have not sat with worthless men, nor will I go in among those who hide what they are.
4.amp: I have not sat [yashab] with vain [shav -- empty, false] persons, neither will I go in [bo] with dissemblers [alam -- the concealed, hypocrites].
4.notes: lo-yashabti im-mete-shav (H3427, H7723): I have not sat with men of shav, emptiness -- the company one keeps as evidence, Psalm 1:1's progression in reverse; ve-im naalamim lo abo (H5956, H935): and with the naalamim, the hidden ones -- men whose real selves are concealed -- I will not go in. Integrity is partly a seating chart.

5.text: I have hated the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the wicked.
5.amp: I have hated [sane] the congregation [qahal -- assembly] of evil doers [raa]; and will not sit [yashab] with the wicked [rasha].
5.notes: saneti qehal mereim (H8130, H6951, H7489): I have hated the qahal of evildoers -- qahal, the word for Israel's own assembly, here a counter-congregation; ve-im-reshaim lo esheb (H7563, H3427): and with the wicked I will not sit. The negative membership list ends; verse 6 gives the positive one.

6.text: I will wash my hands in innocence, and so I will go around Your altar, O LORD,
6.amp: I will wash [rachats] mine hands [kaph -- palms] in innocency: so will I compass [sabab -- go around] Your altar [mizbeach], O LORD [YHWH]:
6.notes: erchats be-niqqayon kappai (H7364, H3709): I wash my palms in innocence -- the priests' laver-rite (Exodus 30:19-21) made a layman's confession; va-asobebah et-mizbachakha YHWH (H5437, H4196, H3068): and I circle Your altar. Pilate's basin (Matthew 27:24) is this gesture emptied; David's is the real thing, and he wants to be near the altar, not away from a crowd.

7.text: to make the voice of thanksgiving heard, and to tell of all Your wonders.
7.amp: That I may publish [shama -- make heard] with the voice [qol] of thanksgiving [todah], and tell [saphar -- recount] of all Your wondrous works [pala -- wonders].
7.notes: lashmia be-qol todah (H8085, H6963, H8426): to make the voice of todah heard -- the thank-offering's song -- u-le-sapper kol-niphleotekha (H5608, H6381): and to recount all Your wonders, Psalm 9:1's verb. The purpose of the clean hands and the circuit of the altar: a testimony, out loud, in public.

8.text: O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory has its tent.
8.amp: LORD [YHWH], I have loved [ahab] the habitation [maon -- dwelling] of Your house [bayith], and the place [maqom] where Your honour ['of the tabernacle of thy honour', mishkan, the KJV margin] dwells.
8.notes: YHWH ahabti meon betekha (H3068, H157, H4583, H1004): LORD, I have LOVED the dwelling of Your house -- u-meqom mishkan kebodekha (H4725, H4908, H3519): the place of the mishkan, the tabernacle, of Your glory -- the margin's literal. The psalm of the separated man is a love song to a building, because of Who is in it (cf. Psalm 27:4; 84:1).

9.text: Do not sweep my soul away with sinners, nor my life with men of blood,
9.amp: Gather ['Take not away', asaph, the KJV margin] not my soul [nephesh] with sinners [chatta], nor my life [chay] with bloody ['men of blood', dam, the KJV margin] men [enosh]:
9.notes: al-teesoph im-chattaim naphshi (H622, H2400, H5315): do not GATHER my soul -- asaph, the gathering-verb, used of the harvest and of a man 'gathered to his people' at death (Genesis 25:8), the margin's 'take away' -- with sinners. ve-im-anshe damim chayyai (H582, H1818, H2416): nor my life with men of bloods -- damim, the Hebrew plural behind the margin's 'men of blood'. The fear behind the whole plea for a verdict: to be swept up in the wrong harvest (cf. Genesis 18:23).

10.text: in whose hands is a wicked scheme, and whose right hand is filled with bribes.
10.amp: In whose hands [yad] is mischief [zimmah -- evil scheme, wickedness], and their right hand [yamin] is full ['filled with', male, the KJV margin] of bribes [shochad].
10.notes: asher-bidehem zimmah (H3027, H2154): in whose hands is zimmah -- a planned wickedness, the word Leviticus uses for sexual crime (Leviticus 18:17). vi-minam maleah shochad (H3225, H4390, H7810): and their right hand -- the hand of oaths and of giving -- is filled, the margin's literal, with shochad, the bribe Deuteronomy 16:19 says blinds the wise. Verse 6's washed palms against verse 10's stuffed ones.

11.text: But as for me, I will walk in my integrity; ransom me, and be gracious to me.
11.amp: But as for me, I will walk [yalak] in mine integrity [tom]: redeem [padah -- ransom] me, and be merciful [chanan -- be gracious] unto me.
11.notes: va-ani be-tummi elekh (H8537, H3212): 'and I' -- the emphatic pronoun -- will walk in my integrity, verse 1's claim now a resolve; pedeni ve-chonneni (H6299, H2603): RANSOM me and be gracious to me. The man of integrity still asks to be bought back and shown grace: the psalm's integrity is a direction of walking, not a claim of sinlessness.

12.text: My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless the LORD.
12.amp: My foot [regel] stands [amad] in an even place [mishor -- level ground]: in the congregations will I bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH].
12.notes: ragli amedah be-mishor (H7272, H5975, H4334): my foot stands on the mishor, the level place -- the answer to verse 1's 'I shall not slide'; be-maqhelim abarekh YHWH (H1288, H3068): in the assemblies I will bless the LORD -- the qahal of verse 5 he refused, exchanged for the congregations where he belongs. He began asking for a verdict and ends in church.
